thesis: COLM has already run from about 61 to 72.26 in two weeks and sits 1% under its 52-week high, RSI 73 and 11.8% above SMA20, so the post-earnings move is largely priced in. The price is at the 73.0 mean analyst target and valuation is only fair (P/E 15.95), leaving little upside to consensus, and the 1.85 reward/risk is only achievable on a pullback entry that has not happened. The earnings jump came from margins (net income +63%) on only +2% revenue, which is a lower-quality driver whose source is unconfirmed because the news feed was down. The regime is risk-off with QQQ below its 50- and 200-day averages, so a stretched, 19% short-interest name is exposed to a sharp reversal if the market sells off or the squeeze fades. Event risk cannot be cleared today with no news check.
